statement: Let X have N elements and G = Sym(X). Let M1, . . . , Mr be disjoint nonempty subsets of X, where r ≥ 1, and put Hi = Sym(Mi), fixing the complement pointwise. Their union need not be X. Suppose f ≥ 0 has mass z ≤ 1 and f(gHi) ≤ K[G : Hi]−1 (g ∈ G, 1 ≤ i ≤ r) for some K ≥ 0. For an irreducible unitary representation ρ of degree D, set Si(D) = X τ∈ b Hi dim τ≤D1/r (dim τ)2 . For every u > 0, the separate orbit and isotypic estimates are ∥ b f(ρ)∥op ≤ zK D X i Si(D) !1/2 ≤ p zKrCu D−1/2+(u+2)/(2r) , (11.1) ∥ b f(ρ)∥2 HS ≤ zK D X i Si(D) ≤ zKrCuD−1+(u+2)/r . (11.2) In particular, when r > 4, the inverse-square orbit estimate gives ∥ b f(ρ)∥op ≤ p rKC2 D−(1−4/r)/2 . (11.3) A separate coefficient-projection argument gives ∥ b f(ρ)∥2 HS ≤ K2 D r X i=1 X τ∈ b Hi dim τ≤D1/r (dim τ)2 ≤ K2 rC10D−1+12/r . (11.4) 32 Finally, for ρ = ρλ with λ ⊢ N, put kλ = N − max(λ1, λ′ 1), M(k) = k X j=0 p(j), where p(j) is the partition number and p(0) = 1. The branching refinement is ∥ b f(ρλ)∥2 HS ≤ zKrM(kλ)D−1+2/r . (11.5) All these statements allow unequal support sizes and unrestricted restriction multiplicities. In particular they include the probability-law cases z = 1.
